en: The Therāpadāna:
Bodhivandanavagga 1.
The Apadāna of the Elder Bodhivandaka
“Seeing a green pāṭali tree,
a plant growing from the earth,
he placed his joined palms together at one side.”
I paid homage to the Pāṭali tree,
having raised my hands in añjali and honoring it with a respectful mind.
Pure within and pure without,
perfectly liberated and free from taints—
Vipassī, honored by the world.
I paid homage to the Pāṭali tree, which was an ocean of compassion and wisdom, as if it were the Fully Enlightened One himself standing before me.
In the ninety-first aeon,
because I paid homage to the Bodhi tree,
I do not recall ever being born in an evil state.
This is the fruit of paying homage:
the four analytical knowledges and these eight liberations.
"The six direct knowledges have been realized;
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Bodhivandaka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Bodhivandaka is the first.
